newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom leads New Zealand shares to a firmer close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom leads New Zealand shares to a firmer close.

text.p: * NZ shares end higher as Telecom extends gains
* Profit-taking seen in Telecom after Salomon downgrade
* Volumes moderate while major offshore markets on holiday
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +10.47 at 2,321.52
319 +1 * NZMC cap index +3.12 at 1,859.43 364 -1 * Volume NZ$45 million. Futures +4 at 1,169
New Zealand shares closed firmer on Tuesday as Telecom extended its gains, but brokers warned the market leader may encounter profit-taking when the major offshore markets return from their holidays.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 10.47 points higher at 2,321.52, with Telecom up nine cents at NZ$6.99.

Telecom has prospered since the second stage of its NZ$1 billion share repurchase programme began, but brokers said the stock's downgrade by heavyweight investment house Salomon Brothers to a 'hold' from a 'buy' would not go unnoticed.

"Telecom closed on Friday before the big markets went to sleep at $6.84 here, so they're going to come back to their offices tonight and see that the stock is up 14 cents," said Don Turkington at Cavill White.
"So you may get some selling coming out, and the Salomon report may encourage that."
Salomon downgraded Telecom on Tuesday because it said "the upturn in the company's business appears to be moving further into the future".

Meanwhile, Carter Holt Harvey made good ground, rising three cents to $3.31, while Brierley slipped a cent to $1.34. Fletcher Paper, up one at $3.19, led the turnover table with 1.69 million shares traded.

Outside the leaders, Progressive Enterprises gained seven to $1.57, and Cultus Petroleum continued to soar following encouraging reports on various oil drilling projects in Australasia, up a further 10 cents to $3.70.
Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said activity was expected to pick up on Wednesday after London and New York re-entered the fray.
